body:
This was an intentional change: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/87756

Copy pasting reasoning which was in another separate PR.

>There are several reasons why most (if not all) 3D software do not transform things by default when clicking anywhere on the viewport.

>It would reintroduce: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/87608

>It would make functionality like https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/102176 a lot less intuitive since you'll have to constantly switch modes, and I believe a lot of future functionality will depend on this one, such as https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/106835

>There are already proven solutions to this that I believe should just not be custom: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/78148 and https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/11926

@ryevdokimov Thanks for pointing out the PR. Although I don't really understand why these tools still exist if I have to hit the 3D object here anyway. (Which I didn't really want to do for convenience's sake, just to quickly build a scene.) In general, you can do everything here with the standard tool. Is there perhaps a way to make a setting out of this?
Yes i can use the "alt" key option, would be fine for me, but here i can not combinate it with"x/y/z" to lock the axis.

I think this will take some time: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/78148
This would also be fine: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/105809 (w -> g)

There are a lot of open discussions, should i close this issue?

I can agree that the apparent differences seem to be less obvious, but there are still valid reasons for their existence for people who prefer a gizmo-based workflow.

The main ones being what the plane transforms do, what dragging on the geometry does, and just removing chances for accidentally selecting the wrong handles. 

>There are a lot of open discussions, should i close this issue?

I personally think it's fine to keep this issue open, there may be further discussions on this topic and its better to keep it in an issue rather than scattered across various PRs.
